function: Joint optimization of RIS phase shifts and BS precoder to maximize weighted sum rate, with a complex-valued phase network and an Euler-update precoder network (pp. 1-3).
system: MU-MISO downlink; BS with M=64 antennas (default), K single-antenna users (K not stated), reflective RIS with N=100 elements, no direct link, 28 GHz (pp. 1, 4).
method: Meta-learning NNs: complex-valued phase network and precoder network (one hidden layer of 200 neurons each), Riemannian Adam; unsupervised loss, negative weighted sum rate (pp. 2-3).
data_channel: Simulated Rician fading (Rician coefficient 10) for BS-RIS and RIS-user links, 3GPP path loss; setup of [4] and [12]; results averaged over 100 channel realizations (pp. 3-4).
test_conditions: No separate training and test sets described: weights randomly initialized, algorithm run for 100 channel realizations and averaged; sweeps over power, N, M; no unseen scenario (pp. 3-5).
baselines: Non-learned: alternating optimization with WMMSE precoder and Riemannian conjugate gradient phases [14]. Learned: GMML [4], plus GAMN-real (real-valued ablation) (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Weighted sum rate (bps) versus epochs, transmit power, number of RIS elements N and BS antennas M; epochs to converge; power gain in dB (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Order O(Ne No Ni K^2 M N) multiplications, same as [4], no matrix inversion; no runtime or parameter count reported (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 3: "assumed to follow Rician fading"; p. 4: "The path loss is set according to the 3GPP standard for LoS and NLoS components". Custom Rician simulator with only the path loss from 3GPP (TS 36.814); no 3GPP TR 38.901 channel model, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "We also run the algorithm for 100 channel realizations and average our results". Algorithm 1 (p. 3) starts from "Randomly initialize" weights; no separate training scenario or unseen scenario is described, and power, N and M are only swept (pp. 4-5).
q3_support: p. 5: "GAMN outperforms GMML by a weighted sum rate difference of 0.7 bps" (earlier learned method [4]); p. 5: "GAMN outperforms the traditional AO baseline by 0.86 bps" (non-learned AO of [14]).
q4_support: p. 5: "the total computational complexity becomes O(Ne No Ni K 2 M N )", i.e. order of complexity of the proposed method, stated to be the same as [4].
q5_support: p. 3: "we set the same channel parameters and setup as in [4] and [12]". The paper gives no code link or DOI, and its channels are simulated, not a public dataset or measured data.
notes: Preprint arXiv:2409.11270v2. Included as learned (meta-learning NNs trained by backpropagation of the negative weighted sum rate), but borderline against no_learning: Algorithm 1 (p. 3) randomly initializes the weights and runs nM=500 epochs per run, and the paper describes no offline training set. K is not stated. 3GPP is cited only for path loss. Power is given as 10 dB in one place and 10 dBm in another (p. 4).
